cond_0001.intro: As an Intermediate Cybersecurity Analyst contracted to support the Integrated Early Warning of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) Sensors project for the Department of Defense (DoD), you will help ensure the security and compliance of software systems critical to national defense. You will work with senior cybersecurity analysts and development teams to conduct security assessments, analyze vulnerabilities, and implement cybersecurity controls. Your responsibilities will include documenting security findings, incident response activities, and compliance efforts for upload to [Product name masked] (Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service) in accordance with DoD standards and regulatory requirements.
cond_0001.responsibilities:

Participating in security assessments of software systems and applications throughout the development lifecycle, identifying vulnerabilities, and recommending mitigation strategies. Collaborating with senior cybersecurity analysts and development teams to integrate security controls and best practices into the design, development, testing, and deployment phases. Assisting in performing threat modeling exercises to identify potential risks and vulnerabilities in software architectures and functionalities. Supporting code reviews and conducting static and dynamic analysis to identify security flaws, coding errors, and vulnerabilities. Assisting in incident response efforts related to cybersecurity incidents and breaches during test events, conducting forensic investigations, and analyzing root causes. Participating in security reviews, audits, and compliance assessments, documenting assessment results and recommendations for remediation. Monitoring security alerts and threat intelligence feeds, assisting in analyzing threat intelligence data, and proactively mitigating risks to software systems. Assisting in documenting security documentation for upload to [Product name masked], ensuring accuracy, completeness, and compliance with DoD reporting requirements. Collaborating with DoD stakeholders, program managers, and security teams, documenting security requirements, concerns, and resolutions to support the successful delivery of software solutions.

Computer, Phone, and basic office materials.
Physical Activities:
Support for cybersecurity testing events in person.

cond_0085.intro:
At [Company name masked], we deliver decision support tools critical for the protection of forces when threatened by both physical and Chemical, Biological, Radiological, or Nuclear (CBRN) threats.
As an Intermediate Cybersecurity Analyst contracted to support the Integrated Early Warning of Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) Sensors project for the Department of Defense (DoD), you will help ensure the security and compliance of software systems critical to national defense. You will collaborate with senior cybersecurity analysts and development teams to conduct security assessments, analyze vulnerabilities, and implement cybersecurity controls. Your responsibilities will include documenting security findings, incident response activities, and compliance efforts for upload to [Product name masked] (Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service) in accordance with DoD standards and regulatory requirements. People who do well in this role are often quick to grasp the logic of DoD cybersecurity frameworks and how they apply to software systems.
cond_0085.responsibilities:
Major Job Activities:
Participating in security assessments of software systems and applications throughout the development lifecycle, identifying vulnerabilities, and recommending mitigation strategies. Collaborating with senior cybersecurity analysts and development teams to integrate security controls and best practices into the design, development, testing, and deployment phases. Assisting in performing threat modeling exercises to identify potential risks and vulnerabilities in software architectures and functionalities. Supporting code reviews and conducting static and dynamic analysis to identify security flaws, coding errors, and vulnerabilities. Assisting in incident response efforts related to cybersecurity incidents and breaches during test events, conducting forensic investigations, and analyzing root causes. Participating in security reviews, audits, and compliance assessments, documenting assessment results and recommendations for remediation. Monitoring security alerts and threat intelligence feeds, assisting in analyzing threat intelligence data, and proactively mitigating risks to software systems. Assisting in documenting security documentation for upload to [Product name masked], ensuring accuracy, completeness, and compliance with DoD reporting requirements. Collaborating with DoD stakeholders, program managers, and security teams, documenting security requirements, concerns, and resolutions to support the successful delivery of software solutions.
Material & Equipment Directly Used:
Computer, Phone, and basic office materials.
Physical Activities:
Support for cybersecurity testing events in person.
cond_0085.requirements:
Active DoD Secret (or higher) level Security Clearance.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or related field. Relevant industry certifications, such as Security+, CySA+, or similar. Demonstrated experience or knowledge in cybersecurity analysis, incident response, and documentation. Familiarity with software development methodologies, coding practices, and secure coding principles. Basic understanding of DoD cybersecurity policies, standards, and directives, with a willingness to learn and adapt to new requirements. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to learn quickly and apply new concepts effectively. Good communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment. Experience working on DoD contracts or within the defense industry. Commitment to maintaining professionalism, integrity, and confidentiality in handling sensitive information.

Your responsibilities will include documenting security findings, incident response activities, and compliance efforts for upload to [Product name masked] (Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service) in accordance with DoD standards and regulatory requirements.
cond_0281.responsibilities:
Major Job Activities:
Participating in security assessments of software systems and applications throughout the development lifecycle, identifying vulnerabilities, and recommending mitigation strategies. Collaborating with senior cybersecurity analysts and development teams to integrate security controls and best practices into the design, development, testing, and deployment phases. Assisting in performing threat modeling exercises to identify potential risks and vulnerabilities in software architectures and functionalities. Supporting code reviews and conducting static and dynamic analysis to identify security flaws, coding errors, and vulnerabilities. Assisting in incident response efforts related to cybersecurity incidents and breaches during test events, conducting forensic investigations, and analyzing root causes. Participating in security reviews, audits, and compliance assessments, documenting assessment results and recommendations for remediation. Monitoring security alerts and threat intelligence feeds, assisting in analyzing threat intelligence data, and proactively mitigating risks to software systems. Assisting in documenting security documentation for upload to [Product name masked], ensuring accuracy, completeness, and compliance with DoD reporting requirements. Collaborating with DoD stakeholders, program managers, and security teams, documenting security requirements, concerns, and resolutions to support the successful delivery of software solutions.
Material & Equipment Directly Used:
Computer, Phone, and basic office materials.
Physical Activities:
Support for cybersecurity testing events in person.
cond_0281.requirements:
Education / Certifications:
Clearance Requirement:
Active DoD Secret (or higher) level Security Clearance.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or related field required; advanced degree strongly preferred. Relevant industry certifications, such as Security+, CySA+, or similar, required. Demonstrated expertise in cybersecurity analysis, incident response, and documentation. Solid understanding of software development methodologies, coding practices, and secure coding principles. Advanced knowledge of DoD cybersecurity policies, standards, and directives, with the ability to apply and adapt to evolving requirements. Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with a proven ability to rapidly apply new concepts in demanding environments. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively and collaboratively across teams. Substantial experience working on DoD contracts or within the defense industry. Proven track record of maintaining professionalism, integrity, and confidentiality when handling sensitive information.
